intro.data: You can hold data two ways: a List (many items) or an Optional (maybe one). safeHead converts any List into an Optional — keep the first item, or nothing if the list is empty. The trick: it has to read the SAME way for every kind of data — Lists of Users, Lists of Emails, all of it. On the left, pick the safeHead converter for each one.
intro.alchemy: You can hold a material two ways: a Batch (many pieces) or a Trace (maybe a speck). Sample draws one piece from any Batch into a Trace — the first, or nothing if the Batch is empty. The trick: the method must work the SAME way for every material — Batches of Herbs, Batches of Essences, all of them. On the left, pick the Sample method for each.
intro.spellcraft: You can bind an essence two ways: a Swarm (many) or an Echo (maybe one). Catch pulls one from any Swarm into an Echo — the first, or nothing if the Swarm is empty. The trick: the working must read the SAME way for every essence — Swarms of Runes, Swarms of Sparks, all of them. On the left, choose the Catch working for each.
intro.abstract: Two functors F, G : C → D are given. A natural transformation α : F ⇒ G is a single arrow between them: a component α_A : F(A) → G(A) at every object A. Choose the component at each object.

goal.data: Pick the safeHead converter for both the User list and the Email list.
goal.alchemy: Pick the Sample method for both the Herb batch and the Essence batch.
goal.spellcraft: Choose the Catch working for both the Rune swarm and the Spark swarm.
goal.abstract: At each object, choose the component α_A : F(A) → G(A).

afterSuccess.data: You picked safeHead for every kind of data — one rule that turns any List into an Optional the same way everywhere. That single, uniform rule is what we call a natural transformation.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You picked Sample for every material — one method that draws from any Batch into a Trace the same way everywhere. That single, uniform rule is what we call a natural transformation.

afterSuccess.abstract: You chose a component at every object — together they form a natural transformation α : F ⇒ G.

reveal.summary: A natural transformation α : F ⇒ G is a family of components α_A : F(A) → G(A), one for every object A — a single arrow between two functors.
reveal.moreFormal: The components must satisfy the naturality condition (next puzzle). Natural transformations are the morphisms of the functor category [C, D]; functors are its objects.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: safeHead<A>: List<A> => Optional<A> — one polymorphic function, all types at once.
